name: Middle East & Central Asia
blurb: Deserts, steppe and mountains where water is scarce: shrinking seas, overgrazed grassland, wildfires, flaring oil fields and the wild forests where the apple began.

issues.title: The Vanishing Aral Sea

drivers.name: Salty, polluted dust from the dry seabed

sites: River forest where Bukhara deer live

fact.text: NASA satellite images show the Aral Sea was already a fraction of its 1960 extent by 2000, after rivers were diverted to farms for cotton and other crops; in 2014 the eastern lobe of the South Aral Sea disappeared completely.
fact.source: NASA Earth Observatory, World of Change: Shrinking Aral Sea

issues.realWorld: Check where cotton clothing comes from, prefer products that report water use, and support delta restoration charities.

issues.title: The Overgrazed Steppe

drivers.name: Mines and roads that cut the grassland

fact.text: A 2014 satellite study in Global Change Biology found that vegetation across Mongolia had declined by about 12% on average, and that about 80% of the decline could be attributed to more livestock; about 70% of the steppe is considered degraded.
fact.source: Hilker et al., Global Change Biology (2014)

also.source: Oregon State University, via ScienceDaily (5 September 2013)

issues.realWorld: Buy wool and cashmere with traceable, sustainable-grazing certification and ask brands how they manage herd sizes.

issues.title: Flares over the Gulf

drivers.name: Flaring of gas from oil wells

sites: A village beside an oil field

fact.text: The World Bank’s Global Gas Flaring Tracker names Iraq among the nine largest gas-flaring countries in 2024; together they accounted for 83% of all gas flared.
fact.source: World Bank, Global Gas Flaring Tracker (2024 data)

issues.realWorld: Cut your own fossil-fuel use where you can, and support groups that track flaring and oil spills with satellite data.

issues.title: A Refuge on the Red Sea

fact.text: Corals in the Gulf of Aqaba endured an exceptional 113-day marine heatwave in 2024, peaking at 32.6°C, and five kinds of coral survived it without bleaching; researchers warn the refuge may be approaching its limit.
fact.source: Kochman and Fine, Science of the Total Environment (2025)

also.source: Hebrew University press release, via EurekAlert

issues.realWorld: Never touch or stand on coral when diving, and choose dive operators that follow a reef-protection code.

issues.title: The Saiga Die-Off

drivers.name: Hot, humid spring weather before outbreaks
Fences and roads that fragment the range

sites: A calving ground in central Kazakhstan

fact.text: In 2015 a mass die-off of about 200,000 saiga antelopes in central Kazakhstan was caused primarily by the bacterium Pasteurella multocida serotype B.
fact.source: Emerging Infectious Diseases (CDC): “Mass Die-Off of Saiga Antelopes, Kazakhstan, 2015” (2019)

issues.realWorld: Support saiga conservation groups, and if you handle livestock or travel to rural areas, follow animal-disease rules on moving animals and reporting sick ones.

issues.title: Fire Season in the Pine Forests

drivers.name: Clearing and arson at the forest edge

sites: A village at the forest edge

fact.text: A 2024 study in Natural Hazards documented Türkiye’s unprecedented 2021 forest fires: 30 large fires affected 164,658 hectares across the Mediterranean, Aegean and Eastern Anatolian regions.
fact.source: Remote sensing and GIS-based inventory of the 2021 forest fires in Türkiye, Natural Hazards (2024)

issues.realWorld: Follow local fire-danger rules and never light fires or throw cigarettes in dry woodland, and support or volunteer with local fire-prevention and reforestation groups.

issues.title: The Birthplace of the Apple

drivers.name: Land conversion for farms and pastures

sites: A wild apple forest in the Tien Shan
A village at the forest edge

fact.text: Wild apple forests in the Tian Shan, home of the main wild ancestor of the cultivated apple, are shrinking, mainly because of clearing for housing and farming and deforestation.
fact.source: Apples and People, “Fruit of the Heavenly Mountains”

issues.realWorld: Choose varied, locally grown apples, support orchards and seed banks that keep old varieties, and back groups protecting wild fruit forests.
